Serve the project over HTTP.

What is served is decided from the project itself. A SITE — `pages/` or `static/` and no `Serve` backend — gets the dev server: largo owns the public port, serves the built pages and assets with hot reload, and answers anything else 404 as a static host would. A FULL-STACK site adds its `Serve` backend as a child on `LOGOS_PORT`, proxied for everything the pages do not answer. A BACKEND — a `Serve` program alone — is interpreted directly and binds its own port. Any other program is built to WebAssembly and served as a bundle.

# Example

```bash largo serve ```

Usage: largo serve [OPTIONS] [ARGS]...

Arguments:
  [ARGS]...
          Arguments to pass to the program (readable via `args()`)

Options:
      --timeout <DURATION>
          Kill the server after this wall clock (`500ms`, `10s`, `2m`)

      --seed <SEED>
          Scheduler seed for deterministic runs (sets LOGOS_SEED)

      --watch
          Serve a program's WebAssembly bundle, rebuilding and live-reloading the browser on every source save. (A site always watches.)

      --open
          Open the served site in your default browser (best-effort)

      --host <ADDR>
          Bind address for a site. Default `127.0.0.1` (this machine only); pass `0.0.0.0` to serve the whole local network, so a phone or a tablet on the same wifi can open the site

      --port <PORT>
          The public port for a site or a bundle (falls forward to the next free port if taken). Default 8080

  -q, --quiet
          Suppress informational output (errors still print)

  -v, --verbose...
          Increase output verbosity (repeatable)

      --color <WHEN>
          When to use terminal colors

          Possible values:
          - auto:   Color when stdout/stderr is a terminal and `NO_COLOR` is unset
          - always: Always emit ANSI, even into pipes (CI logs, `less -R`)
          - never:  Never emit ANSI
          
          [default: auto]

  -h, --help
          Print help (see a summary with '-h')

Examples:
  largo serve                  # site, full-stack site, or backend — decided by the project
  largo serve --port 3000
  largo serve --open           # …and open it in your browser
  largo serve --host 0.0.0.0   # reachable from a phone on the same network
  largo serve --timeout 30s
  largo serve --watch          # a program's bundle, rebuilt + live-reloaded on save
